ios.desc:
Bram's Reading App is a toolkit for becoming a serious reader. Build a personal library, ask better questions, and turn notes into a connected system of ideas.

**Core ideas**
• Questions before completion
• Annotations that deepen understanding
• Parallel reading to make connections faster

**What you can do**
• Add books and track progress at a glance
• Capture annotations quickly (including from the Share Sheet)
• Link notes to questions and revisit what matters
• Add characters, events, and settings to your book, along with their relationships
• Find similar annotations across different books
• Run timed reading sessions with a Live Activity timer
• See your reading streaks with an annotation heatmap
• Search books and annotations in one place
• Explore a methodology for reading as a system
• Add widgets for quick capture and selected books
• Visually traverse your library with Quiz and Explore

Whether you’re reading one great book or five at once, Bram’s Reading App helps you stay curious, intentional, and consistent.

show_hn.title: Show HN: A Question and Annotation Driven Parallel Reading App

quotes.text:
I run a book club where the club members read 60 books a year (https://www.sixtybooksayear.com/). When reading at a pace of ~5 books/month, there are skills you develop to increase your storage of concepts from any given book, but also your ability to synthesize ideas across books.

I've compiled some of my best working knowledge into this app on how to become a serious reader. Bram's Reading App will help you: (1) set questions you want answered before you even pick up a book [Questions Over Completion], (2) answer those questions as you read with deliberate annotations [Commonbase], and (3) learn to read and manage multiple books at the same time [Discursive Reading].

Other Features include: Widgets and Control Center Shortcuts, Save from Share Sheet, Configurable Per Book Reading Notifications, Vector Embedded Annotations Across Books, Reading Sessions with Live Timers, A Tactile Progress Wheel, Nested Commentary, Full Text Search, Quiz Mode (next release), Micro Essay Builder (future release)

I hope you enjoy, and let me know if you have any great tips about being well read!
